question: Does the assembled timer candidate improve startup and complete Go Pipe shop70 execution relative to current main?
scope: Both SQL clock correction and bounded probe omission vs unmodified main, not isolation of the probe alone. Single local Mac; no pgmem/new Ubuntu performance.
workload: Existing immutable timer_calibration runner; 16MiB buffer pool/read1; GOMAXPROCS8 GOGC100; no internal observers. 50 shared-child reads +20 private-child writes, cap=P+1, P4/P8.

sampling.tail_policy: retain every sample, no outcome-selected repeats

baseline_negative_control: Baseline ANALYZE may report zero (known defect); require valid SQL rows, subsequent SELECT and cleanup. Candidate delayed report must be [18, client wall+5]ms.
